## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` re-exports 7 names it does not define, each marked
`# noqa: F401  (re-exported for back-compat)` — 3 from `._processors_identity`
(`_rederive_keyring_keys`, `process_key_event`, `process_signature`) and 4 from
`._processors_status` (`_fold_claimed_session`, `_fold_close_metadata`,
`_fold_plan_review_phase`, `process_status`). ADR 0111 forbids internal shims.

Censused on `origin/main` at `50d5a36539d` with an AST pass over `src`, `tests` and
`scripts` that resolves relative imports and scans `ast.Attribute` and string constants
separately. A line-oriented grep is the wrong instrument here and undercounts, because
the two densest importers spell the name inside a multi-line parenthesized statement.

- **4 names have zero importers** and are deleted outright: `_fold_claimed_session`,
  `_fold_close_metadata`, `_fold_plan_review_phase`, `_rederive_keyring_keys`. None is
  used inside `_processors.py` either, so they are dead in both directions.
- `process_key_event` — 1 importer: `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py:19`.
- `process_signature` — 5 sites: `_replay.py:19`,
  `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13`,
  `tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py:15`, `tests/unit/test_signing.py:117`
  and `:133`.
- `process_status` — 6 sites: `_replay.py:19`,
  `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13`, `tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_happy.py:6`,
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`.
- No attribute-style access anywhere. Two string constants name
  `rebar.reducer._processors`; both were read and neither needs editing (see Out of scope).

**`docs/event-schema.md` names 2 moving symbols in a shape no code census can see.** It
locates processors as a bare filename plus symbol — `_processors.py process_status` at
`:234`, `_processors.py _fold_claimed_session` at `:249` — so a census keyed on the
dotted path matches neither. Both go wrong when the re-exports are deleted. Line `:82`
shows the file's own correct form: `reducer/_processors_status.py:_fold_close_metadata`.

## Change

1. Repoint the 3 names that have importers to the modules defining them:
   `process_key_event` and `process_signature` to `rebar.reducer._processors_identity`,
   `process_status` to `rebar.reducer._processors_status`.
2. **Four** importers pull a genuine `_processors` member on the same statement, so they
   split rather than rewrite wholesale:
   - `_replay.py:19` imports 18 names, 3 of which move — from two different siblings, so
     it becomes **three** statements: 15 names stay, `process_key_event` and
     `process_signature` go to `_processors_identity`, `process_status` to
     `_processors_status`.
   - `test_attestations_reducer.py:13` likewise becomes **three**: `attestation_kind` and
     `process_snapshot` stay, `process_signature` and `process_status` move to their
     respective siblings.
   - `test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py:15` and `test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`
     each also import `process_snapshot` (defined at `_processors.py:469`, stays) — two
     statements each.
3. Delete all 7 re-exports. The whole `from ._processors_status import (...)` statement
   goes, since all 4 of its names are re-export-only. The `._processors_identity`
   statement keeps `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring` (`:139`, `:520`),
   `_fold_author_attribution` (`:81`, `:185`, `:296`) and `attestation_kind` (`:508`),
   which carry no `noqa` because `_processors.py` uses them.
4. Extend the held-out oracle `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py`, which
   already covers these modules and sets the convention: assert the re-exports are absent
   AND that the canonical modules still expose them, so it cannot pass vacuously.
5. Add a `docs/release-notes.md` entry naming the 3 moved import paths and their new
   owning module.
6. Correct the 2 stale locators in `docs/event-schema.md` to
   `reducer/_processors_status.py:process_status` (`:234`) and
   `reducer/_processors_status.py:_fold_claimed_session` (`:249`), matching `:82`'s form.

## Testing

No behavior change: every moved name keeps its definition, only its import path moves.
The existing suite is therefore the oracle, with the held-out shim test as the direct
assertion. `make verify` covers the reducer replay suites that exercise `_replay.py`'s
dispatch, the one production consumer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1** `grep -cF 're-exported for back-compat' src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`
      prints 0.
- [ ] **AC2** Re-running the AST census reports 0 importers for all 7 names.
- [ ] **AC3** `python -c "from rebar.reducer import _processors as p; assert not any(hasattr(p, n) for n in ['_rederive_keyring_keys','process_key_event','process_signature','_fold_claimed_session','_fold_close_metadata','_fold_plan_review_phase','process_status'])"`
      exits 0.
- [ ] **AC4** `python -c "from rebar.reducer._processors_identity import process_key_event, process_signature; from rebar.reducer._processors_status import process_status"`
      exits 0.
- [ ] **AC5** `python -c "from rebar.reducer._processors import process_snapshot, attestation_kind"`
      exits 0.
- [ ] **AC6** `ruff check src tests` exits 0 with no output.
- [ ] **AC7** `pytest tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py -q` exits 0.
- [ ] **AC8** That file's collected case count is strictly greater than its count on
      `origin/main`, measured with `pytest --collect-only -q` on both.
- [ ] **AC9** `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` lists exactly 12 paths:
      `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py`, the 7 named
      test modules, `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py`,
      `docs/release-notes.md`, `docs/event-schema.md`.
- [ ] **AC10** `docs/release-notes.md` gains an entry naming all 3 moved import paths,
      and that file's only diff is additions.
- [ ] **AC11** `grep -cF '_processors.py process_status' docs/event-schema.md` prints 0.
- [ ] **AC12** `grep -cF '_processors.py _fold_claimed_session' docs/event-schema.md`
      prints 0.
- [ ] **AC13** `grep -cF 'reducer/_processors_status.py:process_status' docs/event-schema.md`
      prints 1, and
      `grep -cF 'reducer/_processors_status.py:_fold_claimed_session' docs/event-schema.md`
      prints 1.
- [ ] **AC14** `make verify` exits 0.

## Ordering

Independent of `insanitary-divine-moa` and `peckish-marmatite-cuckoo` — different
modules, no shared file. May land in any order relative to them.

## Out of scope — checked, not merely unexamined

- **`docs/event-schema.md:256`** names `_processors.py _clear_claimed_session`. That
  locator is already wrong on `origin/main`: the symbol is defined at
  `_processors_status.py:35` and was never re-exported. Pre-existing defect, not
  breakage this slice introduces; tracked separately.
- **`attestation_kind`**, imported from `_processors` by 5 files
  (`verify_opcert.py:45`, `_opcert_signing.py:354` and `:437`, `_opcert_verify.py:176`,
  `test_attestations_reducer.py:13`). Not a re-export — used at `:508` — so it stays.
- **`test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:63`** captures logs on logger
  `"rebar.reducer._processors"`, emitted at `_processors.py:495` inside `process_snapshot`,
  which stays. The string remains correct and must not change.
- **`_field_contract.py:114`** prose names `rebar.reducer._processors.process_tag_delta`,
  defined at `_processors.py:434`, which stays.
- Any behavior change in the processors themselves.
